title: Crew of 28 OTU Wellington MF200
memorial_type: Plaque on a stone and brass pillar, in a field beside the village hall
memorial_details:
Sand coloured column with a metal plaque on the top

A plaque on a stone and brass pillar stands in a field beside the village hall off Main Street.
inscription: A memorial to the men who lost their lives in the 19th April 1944 Bomber Crash at Normanton on Soar. Names: Flt Officer D.H. King 24, Pilot Officer D.R. Doyle 24, Sgt D. Fretwell 19, Sgt Garrod 22.

sources.title: Normanton on Soar Air Crash - World War Two
Normanton on Soar bomber crash memorial (WMO 264769)

narrative:
Wellington X MF200 of 28 Operational Training Unit took off from Wymeswold for circuit training on 19 April 1944 and crashed at Normanton on Soar. All four men aboard died. The Nottinghamshire Roll of Honour gives the take-off as 02:30 and the crash about 35 minutes later; War Memorials Online gives 02:50 and a crash about 15 minutes after take-off. The sources do not settle which is right. The IBCC records describe it as night training and give no cause.

The pilot, Flying Officer Donald Hugh King, was 24. The Roll of Honour says he had about 1,500 flying hours but only 10 on Wellingtons. With him were Pilot Officer Douglas Robert Doyle, navigator; Sergeant Desmond Fretwell, 19, wireless operator and air gunner; and Sergeant Lawrence Emmerson Garrod, 22, air gunner. IBCC and War Memorials Online give Doyle's age as 24; the Wicklow heritage page says 25.

King is buried at Burton-on-the-Wolds, Doyle at Greystones (Redford) Cemetery in County Wicklow, Fretwell at Bradfield (St Nicholas) churchyard and Garrod at Blyth (Cowpen) Cemetery.
